bottlenecks.reading: What RDDT supplies that is scarce: a large, constantly refreshed corpus of authentic human conversation (10-K Item 1 Content Licensing) used for LLM search and run-time inference, plus intent-rich community audiences for advertisers. Paid adoption in its own numbers: Other revenue (mostly data licensing) was $43M in Q2 2026, +24% y/y, against Ad revenue $762M +64% (Q2 2026 release). Licensing is small next to ads, so the scarce data asset is monetised mostly via ads and is not yet a large separate line.

Traffic dependency: logged-out DAUq grew 27% y/y to 77.7M in Q2 2026 (US +10%, International +41%) while logged-in DAUq grew only 7% to 52.6M (US +1%, 23.1M); growth rests on logged-out, largely search-referred users. Rivals (Google AI answers, ChatGPT/Gemini, named in Item 1) can substitute the answer without the visit, so the shortage RDDT supplies could be bypassed by AI summaries of its own content.

HYPOTHESIS (secondary press, dated at/after results day, not citable as fact): Reddit told shareholders in October 2026 that Google AI search features cut search referrals by more than 1M per week, plans to test mandatory logins in some international markets, and the roughly $60M a year Google licensing deal is nearing expiry with renewal uncertain; OpenAI deal value (~$70M a year) is a third-party estimate.

HYPOTHESIS: capacity to replace the corpus is added by others slowly (competing communities Discord, Facebook Groups, X, and LLM-generated content), but the 10-K lists these as competitors for the same time, so the moat is user-generated depth, not exclusivity; Reddit has sued scrapers (press, unverified), so access control is part of the bottleneck value.

dc MGMT management plans to move Reddit to a logged-in-only experience, with full tests in select non-US markets from Q4 2026; it will keep reporting logged-in and logged-out DAUq by geography for now and is 'evaluating' user reporting (disclosure-change risk).

dc MGMT Q4 guide midpoint = revenue about +40% y/y (38-42%) and adjusted EBITDA margin about 49%; guidance is for Q4 only (no full-year or 2027 guide). Q3 beat its own guide: revenue 895 vs 860-870 and adj EBITDA 402 vs 385-395.

dc RISK Search dependence: organic traffic from Google and other search engines is a main acquisition channel and Google AI features and algorithm changes can cut referrals (10-K Item 1A, 'rely on search engines'); realized in Q3-Q4 2026 per management.
dc RISK AI competition: LLMs and AI answer products (Google, Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic) may substitute for visits to Reddit and for information seeking (10-K Item 1A competition).

dc RISK Advertising concentration: about 94% of 2025 revenue (91% in 2024) is third-party advertising, sensitive to ad budgets, measurement and privacy changes by Apple, Google and Microsoft (10-K Item 1A, advertising and platform changes).

dc RISK Content licensing is small, fixed-fee and renewal-dependent: 'Other revenue' 5.4% of revenue and RPO over one year $62.4m (10-Q Note on revenue); data-use disputes and scraping litigation risk (10-K Item 1A, IP and data).
dc RISK Cloud infrastructure dependence on AWS and Google Cloud with $1.46bn of three-year commitments (10-Q Note Commitments; 10-K Item 1A, outages).
dc RISK Moderation, content and regulatory exposure (privacy, online safety, EU rules, litigation) and dependence on volunteer moderators (10-K Item 1A).

market_direction.reading: Ad budgets keep growing at the scale platforms RDDT names as rivals (FY2025 revenue growth: META +22.2%, GOOGL +15.1%, PINS +15.8%, SNAP +10.6%), and money is moving to measurable lower-funnel outcomes: RDDT says Q3 2026 click volume grew over 50% and conversion volume more than tripled y/y, with pricing outpacing impressions. The other direction is information seeking moving to AI answers: the 10-Q says declining search referral traffic hurt DAUq growth in Q3 2026 and may worsen, and management reports more than 1M fewer referrals per week in October. The ad market is a tailwind; the traffic market is turning against open-web visits.

bottleneck_potential.reading: RDDT owns a scarce, constantly refreshed corpus of human conversation (10-K Item 1 content licensing), but it is not yet a monetised bottleneck: Other revenue (mostly licensing) was $48.0M in Q3 2026 (+35% y/y from $35.6M), 5.4% of revenue, and remaining performance obligations beyond one year are only $62.4M, so contracts are short and renewal-dependent. The planned move to a logged-in experience is aimed at controlling access to that data (press report of the company's stated aims). How long the scarcity lasts depends on renewals with the same AI firms that compete for the user's question; Google renewal status is only a press hypothesis.

share_trajectory.reading: RDDT is taking ad-budget share on numbers: Q3 2026 revenue $895.0M (+53% y/y), ad revenue $847.0M (+54%), FY2025 revenue +69% against FY2025 growth of META +22.2%, GOOGL +15.1%, PINS +15.8%, SNAP +10.6%. The gain is monetisation, not attention: global DAUq 130.3M (+12% y/y) but US DAUq 50.7M (-2% y/y), US logged-out 27.3M (-4%), US logged-in 23.4M (+1%); US ARPU $13.82 (+53% y/y). International users grew (DAUq 79.6M, +24%) at a low ARPU of $2.43. Peers' Q3 2026 growth was not retrieved, so the comparison is to their FY2025.

competitive_position.reading: Stronger than PINS and SNAP, far smaller and weaker than META and GOOGL. Gross margin 91.5% in Q3 2026 vs FY2025 META 82.0%, PINS 80.1%, SNAP 55.0%; FY2025 operating margin 20.1% (Q3 2026 29.2%) vs PINS 7.6% and SNAP -9.0%, but below META 41.4% and GOOGL 32.0%. Scale: FY2025 revenue $2.2B is about 1.1% of META's $201.0B and 52% of PINS's $4.2B. Its edge is intent-rich, topic-organised conversation (conversion volume tripled y/y); its weakness is that GOOGL is at once a rival for the question, the main traffic source, a licensing customer and a cloud vendor ($580M commitment).

threats.reading: Substitution by AI answers is already happening: search referrals fell meaningfully in Q3 and by more than 1M per week in October, and management said that if the trend continues total DAUq could fall in Q4 by a low double-digit percentage from 130M (a management statement, not a forecast). The 10-Q names LLM answer products from Google, Meta, OpenAI and Anthropic as competitors. The company's own response, a logged-in requirement tested in non-US markets from Q4 2026, may reduce total users and ad reach (10-Q). Other threats: 94% of 2025 revenue is advertising, exposed to platform privacy changes; a securities class action on the Google/AI Overviews impact (motion to dismiss due by 2026-11-23); management is 'evaluating' user reporting (disclosure risk).

bear.event_he: ירידת ההפניות מחיפוש בגוגל נמשכת (יותר ממיליון הפניות פחות בשבוע באוקטובר) והמשתמשים היומיים יורדים בשיעור דו-ספרתי, כפי שההנהלה הזהירה.
המעבר לחוויה עם חובת התחברות, שנבדק מהרבעון הרביעי בשווקים מחוץ לארה"ב, מקטין את מספר המשתמשים ואת החשיפה לפרסומות.
המשתמשים הלא-מחוברים, 59% מהקהל היומי, נשחקים גם בארה"ב (כבר ירידה של 4% בשנה) והעלייה בהכנסה למשתמש לא מפצה.
תגמול במניות עולה (15% מההכנסות ברבעון השלישי) וההתחייבויות לענן (1.46 מיליארד דולר עד 2029) נשארות כשהצמיחה נעצרת, ולכן הרווחיות יורדת.
מפרסמים מקצצים תקציבים בהאטה כלכלית; 94% מההכנסות הן פרסום.

base.event_he: ההכנסות ברבעון הרביעי של 2026 בטווח התחזית, 1.0-1.03 מיליארד דולר (כ-40% צמיחה), ו-EBITDA מתואם של 480-510 מיליון.
ההכנסה למשתמש בארה"ב ממשיכה לעלות (53% ברבעון השלישי) גם כשהקהל האמריקאי לא גדל, והקהל הבינלאומי ממשיך לגדול (24%).
המשתמשים המחוברים ובאפליקציה, שמביאים מעל 80% מההכנסות, ממשיכים לגדול לאט, ולכן ירידת הקהל הלא-מחובר פוגעת פחות בהכנסות.
החברה ממשיכה לקנות מניות בחזרה (340 מיליון דולר בתשעה חודשים, נותרו כ-660 מיליון) כך שמספר המניות נשאר יציב.

bull.event_he: הירידה בקהל היומי נעצרת עד אמצע 2027 והקהל הבינלאומי ממשיך לצמוח מעל 20% בשנה.
הכנסות הרישוי מחברות בינה מלאכותית (כיום כ-5% מההכנסות) גדלות, כי חובת ההתחברות מגינה על התוכן מגריפה ומחזקת את המיקוח מול OpenAI וגוגל.
המינוף התפעולי נמשך: כל דולר הכנסה נוסף מביא כ-54 סנט EBITDA מתואם, והרווח התפעולי מגיע לכ-40%.
הפיד החדש 'בשבילך' מגדיל את זמן השהייה ואת העומס הפרסומי אצל המשתמשים המחוברים.

growth_anchor.reason: No 2027 guidance exists. Base 25%: the Q4 2026 guide midpoint $1,015M is +40% y/y and already includes the warned DAUq drop; Q1-Q2 2027 compare with +69% and +61% quarters, and US growth is all ARPU (+53%) on a US audience down 2%, so growth fades through 2027. Bull 36%: the guided exit rate holds most of the year because logged-in users (over 80% of monetization) keep growing and international DAUq (+24%) and ARPU (+32%) continue. Bear 10%: the low-double-digit DAUq fall persists and spreads, the logged-in-only tests cut reach, and ARPU gains slow to single digits.

mature_margin.reason: EBIT after SBC. Q3 2026 GAAP operating margin was 29.2% after 14.7% SBC; the Q4 guide (adjusted EBITDA about 49% of revenue) less SBC of about 14-15% and negligible D&A implies about 34% GAAP, the base. Bull 40%: incremental adjusted EBITDA margin 53.6% and incremental operating margin 40% keep lifting the margin with scale. Bear 25%: below Q3's 29%, because a shrinking audience removes the operating leverage while SBC (rising in dollars) and the fixed $1.46B cloud commitments stay.

tax_rate.reason: The 2% Q3 rate reflects a full valuation allowance on US deferred tax assets that the 10-Q says may be released within 12 months; the recurring rate normalizes to the US federal 21% plus state taxes (80% of revenue is US). The release itself is a one-time gain kept out of recurring earnings.

terminal_roic.reason: One capital intensity per scenario, from Reddit's operating invested capital (equity less cash and securities; the cash pile is not operating capital): FY2024 290M on revenue 1,300M, FY2025 452M on 2,203M, Q3 2026 580M (incl. 31M leases) on TTM 3,089M; incremental sales-to-capital 5.6 (2024-25) and 9.2 (2025-TTM); receivables are 23.6% of TTM revenue (receivables-only bound about 4.2); capex 0.2-0.3% of revenue. Return on that capital at a normalized 22% tax (not the 2% valuation-allowance rate): FY2025 345M NOPAT on average capital 371M = 0.93; TTM 708M on 580M = 1.22. terminal_roic = the company_path roic of the same scenario (bear 0.30, base 0.95, bull 1.00) and sales_to_capital = that roic / (mature margin x (1 - 22%)), so the DCF reinvestment and the yearly price path rest on the same return. Base 0.95 sits between FY2025 and TTM; bull 1.00: the TTM 1.22 capped at the valuation's 100% limit; bear 0.30 assumes the logged-in transition, product spend and M&A (a stated capital priority) need about three times the evidenced capital per dollar of sales (unproven, a stress).

sales_to_capital.reason: One capital intensity per scenario, from Reddit's operating invested capital (equity less cash and securities; the cash pile is not operating capital): FY2024 290M on revenue 1,300M, FY2025 452M on 2,203M, Q3 2026 580M (incl. 31M leases) on TTM 3,089M; incremental sales-to-capital 5.6 (2024-25) and 9.2 (2025-TTM); receivables are 23.6% of TTM revenue (receivables-only bound about 4.2); capex 0.2-0.3% of revenue. Return on that capital at a normalized 22% tax (not the 2% valuation-allowance rate): FY2025 345M NOPAT on average capital 371M = 0.93; TTM 708M on 580M = 1.22. terminal_roic = the company_path roic of the same scenario (bear 0.30, base 0.95, bull 1.00) and sales_to_capital = that roic / (mature margin x (1 - 22%)), so the DCF reinvestment and the yearly price path rest on the same return. Base 0.95 sits between FY2025 and TTM; bull 1.00: the TTM 1.22 capped at the valuation's 100% limit; bear 0.30 assumes the logged-in transition, product spend and M&A (a stated capital priority) need about three times the evidenced capital per dollar of sales (unproven, a stress).

terminal_growth.reason: Bear only (base and bull stay on the engine rule). The bear is a shrinking audience: search referrals down more than 1M a week in October, US logged-out DAUq down y/y (28.5M to 27.3M), management's warned low-double-digit Q4 fall from 130M total DAUq; logged-out users are 59% of DAUq but under 20% of monetization. A business whose audience shrinks does not grow with nominal GDP forever: after 2041 the bear grows at about inflation (2.5%, no real growth). Multiple test: at the engine's 4.5% the bear's computed forward multiple was 21-22x, above today's ~13x forward (consensus FY2027 EPS) and above the own-history trailing low of 18.7x; this lever brings it inside that range.

bear.reason_he: באוקטובר 2026 ההפניות מחיפוש ירדו בכמיליון בשבוע ומשתמשי ה-US הלא-מחוברים ירדו משנה לשנה (28.5 ל-27.3 מיליון); אם זה נמשך, רדיט תשלם כדי לגדול (שיווק, מוצר, התחייבויות ענן של 1.46 מיליארד דולר שנשארות קבועות), והתשואה יורדת לרמה של התשואה על כל ההון כולל המזומן (כ-20%-30%). תשואה כזו מצדיקה מכפיל נמוך.

base.reason_he: רדיט כמעט לא צריכה הון כדי לגדול: השקעות ציוד של כ-7 מיליון דולר בשנה על הכנסות של מיליארדים, וההון התפעולי (הון עצמי פחות 3.0 מיליארד מזומן) הוא כ-580 מיליון. ב-2025 הרווח התפעולי אחרי מס רגיל היה כ-77% מההון הזה וב-12 החודשים האחרונים כ-124% (רווח תפעולי 908 מיליון). הבסיס לוקח כ-95% - מתחת לשנה האחרונה, כי הצמיחה מאטה (תחזית רבעון 4 מתחת לציפיות) והמס יעלה מ-2% לרמה רגילה. תשואה גבוהה כזו מצדיקה מכפיל גבוה מהשוק.

bull.reason_he: אם המעבר לחוויה מחוברת ולפיד 'בשבילך' מחזיק את המשתמשים, הצמיחה ממשיכה להגיע ממחיר פרסום גבוה יותר למשתמש (ARPU בארה"ב עלה מ-9.04 ל-13.82 דולר ברבעון בשנה) ולא מהשקעות; אז נשמרת התשואה של 12 החודשים האחרונים (כ-122% על ההון התפעולי במס רגיל של 22%; כאן 100%, התקרה של מודל השווי), והמרווח התפעולי ממשיך לעלות (רווח תפעולי ברבעון 3 עלה ל-262 מיליון). זה מצדיק מכפיל גבוה, בתנאי שהשימוש לא נשחק.

own_history.years: 2026-02 to 2026-10 (trailing GAAP P/E, month-end; 2025 values 120-215x were on tiny first earnings and are excluded)

key_risk.reading_he: רדיט תלויה בתנועה מגוגל: 59% מהמשתמשים היומיים אינם מחוברים ורובם מגיעים מחיפוש, ההפניות ירדו ביותר ממיליון בשבוע באוקטובר, וההנהלה הזהירה מירידה דו-ספרתית בקהל ברבעון הרביעי. אם הקהל ממשיך לרדת, העלייה בהכנסה למשתמש לבדה לא תחזיק צמיחה גבוהה.

falsifiers.metric: Q1 2027 revenue, USD (above = bear refuted: the bear's FY2027 +10% implies about 730M at 2026's Q1 share of 19.6%; 800M = +21% y/y on Q1 2026's 663.4M)
Q1 2027 revenue, USD (below = bull's 36% year refuted)
Q4 2026 global DAUq, millions (below = traffic decline not contained)
Q4 2026 logged-in DAUq global, millions (below Q3's 53.5 = logged-in users, over 80% of monetization, no longer growing q/q: base refuted)
Q3 2027 US ARPU, USD per quarter (below 15.20 = less than +10% y/y on Q3 2026's 13.82; base's 25% FY2027 on a flat US audience needs ARPU growth)
Q1 2027 logged-in DAUq global, millions (above 55.0 = logged-in growth holds at least +4% y/y through the logged-in-only tests: bear's reach loss refuted)

moat.note: Moat source evidenced: a unique user-generated, topic-organised corpus and community network (91.5% gross margin, above META 82%, PINS 80%). Not strong: user acquisition depends on GOOGL search referrals that are falling, and logged-in DAUq grew only 6.6% y/y (53.5M vs 50.2M); the same AI products from GOOGL/META/OpenAI can summarise the content without the visit.

switching_costs.note: Advertisers buy in auctions and can move budgets among the platforms the 10-K names (Google, Meta, Snap, TikTok, Pinterest, X); no multi-year ad contracts are disclosed. User-side switching costs (community identity, karma) are not measured in the filings.

pricing_power.note: US ARPU $13.82 vs $9.04 (+53% y/y) and global ARPU +36% with US users flat; management says pricing outpaced impressions in Q3 2026 while conversions tripled, so the price rise is backed by advertiser outcomes. Still an auction price: it falls if conversions or reach weaken.

retention.note: Management cites strong advertiser retention and new-user first-week return up over 50% y/y (management statements, no rates disclosed). Hard numbers are flat in the US: logged-in DAUq 23.4M vs 23.1M, WAUq 188.5M vs 187.8M.

customer_concentration.note: No customer above 10% of revenue and no country other than the US at 10% or more; active mid-market advertisers grew over 50% y/y. The real concentration is the traffic source (Google), assessed under substitutes, and the revenue type (94% advertising).

market_size.note: Headroom relative to named rivals, not a TAM study: RDDT's FY2025 revenue is about 1.1% of META's and 0.5% of GOOGL's; international ARPU $2.43 vs US $13.82 per quarter leaves room if international monetisation catches up.

competition.note: Growing ad revenue about 2-5x faster than META, GOOGL, PINS and SNAP (FY2025 rates) with better margins than PINS and SNAP, but META and GOOGL own far larger audiences, data and ad tooling, and GOOGL controls RDDT's main acquisition channel.

substitutes.note: AI answers (Google AI Overviews/AI Mode, ChatGPT, Gemini, Anthropic) substitute for the logged-out visit: US DAUq -2% y/y, logged-out users are 59% of DAUq (76.8M of 130.3M), referrals down more than 1M per week in October; management warned of a possible low double-digit DAUq fall in Q4.

management.note: Revenue beat its own guidance midpoint in 8 of 8 quarters since Q4 2024 (mean actual/guide 1.10; Q3 2026 1.03, the smallest beat); disclosed the traffic problem early with a sized warning. Caveat: it is 'evaluating' user reporting, a disclosure-change risk.

capital_allocation.note: Buybacks of $340M in 9M 2026 roughly offset SBC of $301M (Q3 SBC $131M = 14.7% of revenue, rising), holding fully diluted shares near 206M; buybacks neutralise dilution rather than shrink the count. Derived ROIC is very high: FY2025 operating income $442M on about $452M invested capital (equity $2,929M less $2,477M cash and securities), because the business needs almost no capital (capex 0.1% of revenue). No debt, $3.03B cash; $1.46B of AWS/Google Cloud commitments through 2029.

governance.note: Multi-class structure (46.2M Class B vs 147.0M Class A) concentrates voting control; Advance Magazine Publishers holds about 22% of shares. No evidenced abuse, but outside holders have limited say.

regulation.note: Exposed to privacy (GDPR, CCPA, FTC), online-safety and content-liability regimes and a securities class action on the Google impact (second amended complaint 2026-10-23; damages unspecified). None is sized as a revenue risk in the filings.

technology_ai.note: ML feeds and ad tools are delivering (conversions tripled, incremental adjusted EBITDA margin 53.6% y/y), and the corpus is licensed to AI firms; but AI is also the main substitution threat and licensing is only 5.4% of revenue.

geopolitics.note: About 80% of revenue is US-billed, no other country at 10%, substantially all long-lived assets in the US, Reddit is not directly accessible in China; tariff exposure is indirect through advertisers and unsized.

cyclical.reason: Four years of history are a scale-up (revenue $667M in 2022 to $2,203M in 2025, operating margin -26% to +20%) with no completed ad cycle; the ads_platform model is not price-cyclical. Ad-budget sensitivity and the search-traffic shock are carried as bear mechanisms, not a cycle-average margin.
